examples.ko: 운동을 마치고 나니 온몸이 땀투성이가 됐어요.
examples.en: After exercising, my whole body was drenched in sweat.
I wiped my sweaty face with a towel.
I rode the bus in summer and now my shirt is soaked with sweat.
The child ran into the house covered in sweat.
Clothes soaked with sweat should be washed right away.
We were all covered in sweat from climbing the mountain.

explain: '땀범벅'이라고도 해요. '-투성이'는 '먼지투성이', '흙투성이'처럼 무언가가 잔뜩 묻거나 가득한 모습에 붙여요. 보통 '땀투성이가 되다', '땀투성이다'로 말해요.
explain_en: People also say '땀범벅'. The ending '-투성이' attaches to words like '먼지투성이' (covered in dust) and '흙투성이' (covered in mud) for something that is smeared on or full of something. It is usually used as '땀투성이가 되다' or '땀투성이다'.

examples.en: I got home around dusk.
As dusk settled in, the lights came on in the street.
I went out for a walk as dusk was falling.
Please come back quickly before dusk falls.
Before I knew it, the twilight had deepened.
We walked slowly in the twilight.

explain: 보통 '땅거미가 지다'라고 짝을 지어 말해요. 일상 대화에서는 '해 질 때', '저녁 무렵'이라고 하는 경우가 많고, '땅거미'는 이야기나 글에서 분위기를 낼 때 어울려요.
explain_en: It is usually paired as '땅거미가 지다' (dusk falls). In daily talk people often say '해 질 때' or '저녁 무렵' instead, and '땅거미' suits stories and writing where you want a mood.

examples.en: It's a bit late, but congratulations.

examples.ko: 그 일은 지금 사과하기엔 이미 때늦어요.
examples.en: It's already too late to apologize for that now.
Out-of-season snow suddenly fell in mid-April.
I found out late, but thank you for helping.
Regret that comes too late is of no use.
It's already too late, so let's do well next time.

explain: '늦다'와 달리 알맞은 시기를 놓쳤다는 느낌이 있어요. '뒤늦다'와 비슷하게 쓰는데, '때늦다'는 해야 할 때가 지나 버렸다는 쪽이에요. '때늦은 후회', '때늦은 감이 있다'처럼 자주 묶어서 써요.
explain_en: Unlike plain '늦다', it carries the feeling that the right moment has been missed. It is close to '뒤늦다', but '때늦다' leans toward the proper time having already passed. It is often used in set phrases like '때늦은 후회' and '때늦은 감이 있다'.

examples.en: On the weekend I got a body scrub at the bathhouse with my mom.

examples.ko: 때밀이 아주머니가 등을 시원하게 밀어 주셨어요.
examples.en: The scrub lady scrubbed my back until it felt refreshing.
How much is a body scrub at this bathhouse?
After the body scrub, my skin feels smooth.
I want to book a body scrub for the first time in a while.
Soak your body first before the body scrub.

explain: 목욕탕에서 때를 밀어 주는 일도 되고 그 일을 하는 사람도 되는 말이에요. 혼자 밀 때는 '때를 밀다'라고 해요. 정중하게는 '세신사'라고도 불러요.
explain_en: It can mean the scrubbing service at a bathhouse or the person who does it. When you scrub yourself, you say '때를 밀다'. A more polite word for the person is '세신사'.

examples.en: I scrubbed my arms and legs with the washcloth.
I bought a scrub cloth at the shop in front of the bathhouse.
The scrub cloth is so rough that it hurts.
Please don't use a scrub cloth on a baby's skin.

examples.ko: 이 때수건은 어디서 살 수 있어요?
examples.en: Where can I buy this scrub cloth?
Could you lend me a scrub cloth?

explain: 목욕할 때 때를 밀려고 쓰는 거친 수건이에요. '이태리타월'이라고도 불러요. 쓰는 동작은 '때를 밀다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is the rough cloth used to scrub off dead skin in the bath. It is also called '이태리타월'. The action of using it is '때를 밀다'.

examples.en: I skipped class today with a friend.
If you skip cram school, your parents will scold you.
I didn't feel like working, so I ditched and watched a movie.
Don't slack off, do your homework first.
Shall we skip out and go have fun?
He often skips out on work.

explain: 친구끼리 편하게 쓰는 구어예요. 선생님이나 윗사람 앞에서는 '결석하다', '빠지다'처럼 말하는 게 좋아요. 수업뿐 아니라 해야 할 일을 빼먹고 놀 때도 써요.
explain_en: It is casual speech used among friends. In front of teachers or elders, it is better to say '결석하다' or '빠지다'. It is used not only for classes but also for slipping away from things you should be doing.

examples.en: Clouds drift slowly across the sky.
The paper boat floated away on the water.
A balloon floated away in the wind.
I watched the clouds drift by for a long time.
Fallen leaves are floating along the river.

examples.ko: 저기 작은 배가 한 척 떠가네요.
examples.en: Look, a little boat is drifting along over there.

explain: '떠내려가다'는 물살에 휩쓸려 아래로 흘러갈 때 쓰고, '떠가다'는 공중이나 물 위에 떠서 잔잔하게 움직일 때 어울려요. 구름, 배, 풍선처럼 가볍게 움직이는 것에 자주 써요.
explain_en: '떠내려가다' is for being swept downstream by a current, while '떠가다' suits something calmly moving along while floating in the air or on water. It fits light things like clouds, boats and balloons.

examples.en: Branches are floating down from upstream.
A lot of trash floated down because of the flood.

examples.ko: 빈 상자가 물에 떠내려오는 걸 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw an empty box floating down the water.
There was a letter inside the bottle floating down.

examples.ko: 큰 비 뒤에 나무가 떠내려와서 다리가 막혔어요.
examples.en: After the heavy rain, trees floated down and blocked the bridge.

examples.ko: 상류에서 배 한 척이 떠내려오고 있어요.
examples.en: A boat is floating down from upstream.

explain: 반대말은 '떠내려가다'예요. '떠내려오다'는 물에 실려 말하는 사람 쪽으로 다가올 때 써요. 강, 홍수, 바다처럼 물과 함께 쓰는 말이에요.
explain_en: Its counterpart is '떠내려가다'. '떠내려오다' is used when something carried by water comes toward the speaker. It goes with water settings such as rivers, floods and the sea.

examples.en: My friend shoved me as a joke.

examples.ko: 부모님의 재촉에 떠밀려 결혼 준비를 시작했어요.
examples.en: Pushed by my parents' urging, I started preparing for marriage.
I got pushed along by the crowd and ended up getting off the subway.
Don't push the work off onto your younger sibling.

examples.ko: 뒤에서 누가 떠미는 바람에 넘어질 뻔했어요.
examples.en: Someone pushed me from behind and I almost fell.
They are passing the responsibility back and forth to each other.

explain: '밀다'보다 힘으로 거칠게 밀어내는 느낌이 있어요. 책임이나 일을 남에게 넘길 때도 쓰고, 비슷한 말로 '떠넘기다'가 있어요. '떠밀려 ~하다'는 어쩔 수 없이 하게 됐다는 뜻으로 자주 써요.
explain_en: It feels rougher and more forceful than plain '밀다'. It is also used when passing off responsibility or work to others, similar to '떠넘기다'. The pattern '떠밀려 ~하다' means being pushed into doing something against your will.

examples.en: Try sounding out what that person really thinks.

examples.ko: 월급을 물어보며 내 마음을 떠보는 것 같았어요.
examples.en: It seemed like he was testing me by asking about my salary.

examples.ko: 친구가 일부러 말을 걸어 나를 떠봤어요.
examples.en: My friend deliberately talked to me to feel me out.
I pretended not to know to test out the price.
Stop testing me and tell me honestly.
It feels bad when you keep probing me.

explain: 상대의 속마음이나 생각을 알아내려고 슬쩍 말이나 행동으로 시험해 볼 때 써요. '눈을 떠 보다'처럼 '뜨다'와 '보다'를 띄어 쓰는 말과는 달라요. 듣는 사람은 기분이 나쁠 수 있어서 '떠보지 마세요'처럼 자주 말해요.
explain_en: It is used when you subtly test someone with words or actions to find out what they really think. It differs from '눈을 떠 보다', where '뜨다' and '보다' are written separately. The other person may feel bad, so people often say '떠보지 마세요'.

examples.en: Fish died en masse in the river.

examples.ko: 뉴스에서 양식장 물고기 떼죽음 소식이 나왔어요.
examples.en: The news reported mass deaths of fish at a fish farm.

examples.ko: 날씨가 갑자기 추워져서 닭이 떼죽음을 했어요.
examples.en: The weather suddenly turned cold and the chickens died in large numbers.
They are investigating the cause of the mass die-off in the lake.

examples.ko: 오염된 물 때문에 조개가 떼죽음 직전이에요.
examples.en: The clams are on the verge of dying en masse because of the polluted water.
They say a mass die-off of pigs happened on the farm.

explain: '떼'는 무리라는 뜻이라 많은 동물이 한꺼번에 죽는 일에 써요. 뉴스에서 물고기, 새, 가축 이야기에 자주 나와요. 보통 '떼죽음을 당하다', '떼죽음이 일어나다'로 말해요.
explain_en: '떼' means a group, so this word is for many animals dying all at once. It shows up in news about fish, birds and livestock. It is usually said as '떼죽음을 당하다' or '떼죽음이 일어나다'.

examples.en: This line doesn't look straight.

examples.ko: 똑바른 자세로 앉아야 허리가 안 아파요.
examples.en: You have to sit up straight so your back doesn't hurt.

examples.ko: 길이 똑바로 이어져 있어서 찾기 쉬워요.
examples.en: The road runs straight, so it's easy to find.

examples.ko: 그 아이는 마음이 똑발라서 거짓말을 안 해요.
examples.en: That child is upright and doesn't tell lies.
Please look me straight in the eye and say it.
I like the line that was drawn straight.

explain: '르 불규칙'이라서 '똑발라요', '똑발라서'로 바뀌어요. '똑바로 서다', '똑바로 보다'처럼 부사 '똑바로'로도 써요. 선이나 자세뿐 아니라 마음이나 태도가 바르다는 뜻으로도 써요.
explain_en: It is a '르' irregular adjective, so it becomes '똑발라요' and '똑발라서'. It is also used as the adverb '똑바로', as in '똑바로 서다' and '똑바로 보다'. Besides lines and posture, it can also describe an upright mind or attitude.

examples.en: The child looked at me with big round eyes.

examples.ko: 오늘 밤 보름달이 똥그래서 정말 예뻐요.
examples.en: The full moon tonight is perfectly round and so pretty.
I bought a doll with a round face.
I was startled and my eyes went wide.
My puppy's eyes are really round.

examples.ko: 똥그랗게 구운 빵이 접시에 놓여 있어요.
examples.en: Round baked bread is sitting on the plate.

explain: '동그랗다'보다 센 느낌을 주는 말이에요. 눈이나 얼굴처럼 작고 귀여운 것에 잘 어울려요. 'ㅎ 불규칙'이라서 '똥그래요', '똥그란'으로 바뀌어요.
explain_en: It has a stronger, more emphatic feel than '동그랗다'. It fits small, cute things such as eyes and faces. It is a 'ㅎ' irregular adjective, so it becomes '똥그래요' and '똥그란'.

examples.en: The children romp happily on the playground.
The puppy frolicked in the yard all day.
I fell while running around and got a bruise on my knee.
Seeing kids play to their heart's content makes me happy.
I wanted to run around, so I suggested going to the park.

examples.ko: 비가 그치자 아이들이 다시 뛰놀기 시작했어요.
examples.en: When the rain stopped, the kids started running around again.

explain: 그냥 '놀다'보다 몸을 많이 움직이며 신나게 노는 모습이에요. 주로 아이나 동물에게 써요. '놀다'처럼 ㄹ이 빠져서 '뛰노는', '뛰노세요'가 돼요.
explain_en: Unlike plain '놀다', it pictures lively play with lots of movement, mostly for children and animals. Like '놀다', the ㄹ drops, giving '뛰노는' and '뛰노세요'.

examples.en: I vaulted over the box in gym class.
The vaulting box was so high that I was scared.
Put your hands on the box and jump over it.
Vaulting over the box is the hardest for me.
Mats and a vaulting box are also ready in the gym.
My friend fell from the vaulting box and got hurt.

explain: 학교 체육 시간에 넘는 운동 기구예요. 보통 '뜀틀을 넘다'라고 말하고, '뜀틀 운동'처럼도 써요. 처음엔 달려가서 구름판을 밟고 넘는 순서로 배워요.
explain_en: It is the apparatus jumped over in school gym class. It is usually said as '뜀틀을 넘다', and also appears as '뜀틀 운동'. Students typically learn it by running up, stepping on the springboard and vaulting over.

examples.ko: 겨울마다 할머니가 손자에게 줄 목도리를 뜨개질하세요.
examples.en: Every winter, my grandmother knits a scarf for her grandson.
My grandmother is very skilled at knitting.
I learned knitting from my grandmother when I was little.
I saw someone knitting on the bus.
On my days off, I knit at a cafe.
When I knit, time passes quickly.

explain: '털실로 목도리를 뜨다'처럼 '뜨다'만 써도 같은 뜻이에요. 보통 '뜨개질을 하다'로 쓰고, 어떤 사람이 잘하면 '뜨개질에 능하다'라고 말해요. 바늘 하나로 뜨는 코바늘 뜨개질도 있어요.
explain_en: You can also use just '뜨다', as in '털실로 목도리를 뜨다', with the same meaning. It is commonly said as '뜨개질을 하다', and for someone skilled, '뜨개질에 능하다'. There is also crochet, done with a single hook, called '코바늘 뜨개질'.

examples.en: I want to eat some piping hot soup.
The floor is nicely hot, so I get sleepy.

examples.ko: 추운 날에는 뜨끈하게 목욕하는 게 최고예요.
examples.en: On cold days, a hot bath is the best.

examples.ko: 이마가 뜨끈한데 열이 있는 것 같아요.
examples.en: My forehead feels hot, so I think I have a fever.
In winter, the floor of the heated room is very warm.
I drank milk that was warmed until hot.

explain: '따뜻하다'보다 꽤 뜨거워서 몸이 풀리는 기분 좋은 느낌이에요. 국물, 목욕, 온돌 바닥처럼 몸을 데우는 것에 잘 어울려요. 구어에서 '뜨끈뜨끈'으로도 말해요.
explain_en: It is hotter than '따뜻하다' and gives a pleasant feeling of the body loosening up. It fits things that warm you, such as soup, a bath and a heated floor. In speech you also hear '뜨끈뜨끈'.

examples.en: His dream is like a pie in the sky.
I spent all my time chasing empty dreams.
Floating clouds drift slowly across the sky.
I feel so sorry for the money that vanished like a cloud.
I drank coffee while watching the clouds drift outside the window.

examples.ko: 인생이 뜬구름 같다고 느낄 때가 있어요.
examples.en: Sometimes I feel that life is like a drifting cloud.

explain: 하늘에 떠 있는 구름을 말하지만, 실제로는 붙잡을 수 없고 허무한 것을 비유할 때 더 많이 써요. '뜬구름 같다'처럼 덧없고 현실성 없는 것에 붙여요. 구름만 가리킬 때는 그냥 '구름'이라고 해도 돼요.

phrases.example: 뜬구름 잡는 소리 말고 현실적인 계획을 말해 봐요.
phrases.en: to talk about vague, unrealistic things
phrases.nuance_ko: 구름을 잡을 수 없듯이 막연하고 현실성 없는 이야기를 한다는 뜻이에요. 보통 '뜬구름 잡는 소리'로 쓰며 상대의 말을 핀잔줄 때가 많아요.
phrases.nuance_en: Just as you cannot grab a cloud, it means talking vaguely and unrealistically. It is usually used as '뜬구름 잡는 소리' and often to scold someone's talk.

explain_en: It literally means a cloud floating in the sky, but it is often used figuratively for something unreachable, fleeting or unrealistic, as in '뜬구름 같다'. If you only mean a cloud, plain '구름' is fine.

examples.en: We tore apart and remodeled the old house into a cafe.
My father took apart and rebuilt the old desk himself.
We have to overhaul the plan from the beginning.

examples.ko: 그 나쁜 버릇을 뜯어고치기가 쉽지 않아요.
examples.en: It isn't easy to completely break that bad habit.
Many people say the system should be overhauled.

examples.ko: 부엌을 뜯어고치는 데 한 달이 걸렸어요.
examples.en: It took a month to completely remodel the kitchen.

explain: 그냥 '고치다'보다 뜯어서 크게 바꾼다는 느낌이 강해요. 집이나 가구 같은 물건뿐 아니라 버릇, 제도, 계획처럼 뿌리부터 바꿀 때도 써요. 작은 수리에는 '고치다'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It feels much bigger than plain '고치다', as if you take something apart and change it greatly. It is used for objects like houses and furniture, and also for changing habits, systems or plans from the root. For small repairs, '고치다' sounds more natural.

examples.en: The referee gave the player a red card.
A player who gets a red card is sent off right away.
A red card came out for a rough foul.
Two yellow cards are the same as a red card.
We lost today's match because of a red card.
That player was sent off with a red card.

explain: 축구 같은 경기에서 반칙을 크게 했을 때 심판이 꺼내는 카드로, 받으면 퇴장해요. 가벼운 경고는 '옐로카드'라고 해요. 보통 '레드카드를 받다', '레드카드를 꺼내다'로 말해요.
explain_en: In sports like soccer, this is the card a referee shows for a serious foul, and the player must leave. A lighter warning is a '옐로카드'. It is usually said as '레드카드를 받다' or '레드카드를 꺼내다'.

examples.en: Grandfather is carrying vegetables on a handcart.
I pulled the handcart up the hill.

examples.ko: 시장 앞에 리어카가 여러 대 서 있어요.
examples.en: Several handcarts are standing in front of the market.
I moved the boxes with a friend using a handcart.
The handcart's wheel came off, so I parked it by the road.

examples.ko: 이 리어카는 짐을 많이 실을 수 있어요.
examples.en: This handcart can carry a lot of load.

explain: 바퀴가 달려 있어서 짐을 싣고 손으로 끄는 수레예요. '수레'라고도 하지만 이런 수레는 '리어카'라고 불러요. '리어카를 끌다'로 말해요.
explain_en: It is a wheeled cart pulled by hand to carry loads. It can also be called '수레', but this kind of cart is called '리어카'. You say '리어카를 끌다' for pulling it.

examples.en: I spread margarine on my bread and ate it.
There was no butter, so I fried it with margarine.
Please keep the margarine in the fridge.
The margarine melted and spread across the pan.
Put one spoonful of margarine in the frying pan.
I bought margarine and flour at the mart.

explain: 버터와 비슷하게 빵에 바르거나 요리에 쓰지만 대개 식물성 기름으로 만들어요. 그래서 '버터' 대신 쓸 수 있는 재료로 이야기해요. 보통 '마가린을 바르다', '마가린을 두르다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is used like butter, for spreading on bread or cooking, but it is generally made from vegetable oil. So people talk about it as something to use instead of '버터'. It is usually said as '마가린을 바르다' or '마가린을 두르다'.

examples.en: The horses are resting in the stable.
I forgot to close the stable door.
There is an old stable next to the farm.
The whole day went by cleaning the stable.

examples.ko: 아침마다 마구간으로 가서 말에게 먹이를 줘요.
examples.en: Every morning I go to the stable and feed the horses.
When it rained, I put the horse in the stable.

explain: 말을 기르는 곳이에요. 소를 기르는 곳은 '외양간'이라고 해서 짝으로 알아 두면 좋아요. 승마장에서도 말이 지내는 곳을 마구간이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is where horses are kept. The place for cows is '외양간', so it helps to learn them as a pair. At riding grounds, the place where horses stay is also called '마구간'.

examples.en: When a volcano erupts, magma rises to the surface.
Magma is deep underground.
When magma cools and hardens, it becomes rock.
The temperature of magma is over a thousand degrees.

examples.ko: 과학 시간에 마그마와 용암의 차이를 배웠어요.
examples.en: In science class, I learned the difference between magma and lava.
He is a scholar who studies the magma underground.

explain: 땅속에 있을 때는 '마그마', 땅 위로 흘러나오면 '용암'이라고 해요. 과학 시간이나 화산 뉴스에서 자주 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 '용암'이 더 익숙하게 들려요.
explain_en: Underground it is '마그마', and once it flows out onto the surface it is called '용암' (lava). It comes up in science class and volcano news. In everyday talk, '용암' may sound more familiar.

examples.en: The wooden floor was cold, so I put on socks.
The child lay down on the wooden floor and fell asleep.
I wiped the wooden floor clean with a rag.
The old wooden floor creaks.

examples.ko: 집 안 마룻바닥은 나무로 되어 있어요.
examples.en: The floor inside the house is made of wood.
I laid a blanket on the wooden floor and slept.

explain: 그냥 '바닥'보다 나무판을 깐 마루의 바닥이라는 느낌이 있어요. 사이시옷이 있어서 '마루빠닥'처럼 소리 나요. 아파트 거실처럼 나무 바닥에는 '마루'나 '마룻바닥'을 써요.
explain_en: Compared with plain '바닥', it suggests the floor of a '마루' laid with wooden boards. Because of the 사이시옷, it is pronounced like '마루빠닥'. For wooden floors such as an apartment living room, '마루' or '마룻바닥' is used.

examples.en: I packed dry side dishes in my lunch box.

examples.ko: 마른반찬은 오래 두고 먹을 수 있어요.
examples.en: Dry side dishes can be kept and eaten for a long time.
The dry side dishes are salty, so I need a lot of rice.

examples.ko: 식탁에 국과 마른반찬 세 가지를 차렸어요.
examples.en: I set the table with soup and three dry side dishes.
Among dry side dishes, stir-fried anchovies taste the best.

examples.ko: 마른반찬만 있어도 밥 한 그릇은 먹어요.
examples.en: I can eat a bowl of rice with just dry side dishes.

explain: 국물이 없는 반찬을 말해요. 멸치볶음이나 김처럼 오래 두고 먹는 반찬이 떠올라요. 반대로 국물이 있는 반찬은 '국물 반찬'이라고 불러요.
explain_en: These are side dishes without broth, such as stir-fried anchovies or seaweed, which keep well. The opposite, side dishes with broth, can be called '국물 반찬'.

examples.en: I was nervous before the presentation and swallowed hard.

examples.ko: 마른침만 꿀꺽 삼키고 말을 못 했어요.
examples.en: I only gulped and couldn't say a word.
I could hear the sound of someone swallowing nervously.
My mouth is so dry that I can't even work up any saliva.
I was nervously swallowing while waiting for the result.
The sound of swallowing nervously was loud.

explain: '마른침'은 거의 '삼키다'와 함께 쓰는 짝말이에요. 긴장하거나 겁이 나거나 기대될 때의 몸 반응을 그릴 때 써요. 입이 바싹 말랐다는 느낌을 함께 줘요.

phrases.example: 결과 발표 전에 모두 마른침을 삼켰어요.
phrases.nuance_ko: 긴장하거나 두렵거나 기대될 때 하는 행동을 표현해요. 실제로 침을 삼킨다는 뜻보다 마음 상태를 나타내는 말로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It expresses what you do when nervous, scared or anticipating something. It describes the state of mind more than the actual act of swallowing saliva.

explain_en: '마른침' is almost always paired with '삼키다'. It describes the body's reaction when you are nervous, scared or full of anticipation. It also gives the feeling that the mouth has gone dry.

examples.ko: 지난 몇 달 동안 마음고생이 심했어요.
examples.en: The past few months have been emotionally very hard.
You look like you've been through a lot emotionally.
After all the emotional hardship, a good result came out.
My parents suffered a lot of worry because of the child.
You've been through a lot all this time. Thank you so much.
I lost a lot of weight because of the emotional stress.

explain: 몸이 힘든 것이 아니라 걱정이나 눈치 때문에 마음이 힘든 걸 말해요. '마음고생(을) 하다', '마음고생이 심하다'로 쓰고, 위로할 때 '마음고생 많았어요'라고 해요. 몸이 힘든 '몸고생'과 같이 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: It refers to hardship felt in the heart because of worry or having to watch others' reactions, not physical hardship. It is used as '마음고생(을) 하다' or '마음고생이 심하다', and to comfort someone you say '마음고생 많았어요'. It is sometimes paired with '몸고생', physical hardship.

examples.en: My father worked as a laborer when he was young.

examples.ko: 공사장에서 막노동꾼 몇 명을 구하고 있어요.
examples.en: The construction site is looking for a few laborers.
You shouldn't look down on someone for being a laborer.

examples.ko: 새벽 인력 사무소에는 막노동꾼이 많이 모여요.
examples.en: Many laborers gather at the labor office at dawn.
He is a laborer by day and a student by night.
The laborers at the construction site also rest at lunchtime.

explain: 기술 없이 몸으로 하는 일을 하는 사람을 말하는데, 듣는 사람에 따라 낮추어 부르는 느낌이 있어요. 직접 부를 때나 정중하게 말할 때는 '일용직 근로자', '노동자'가 더 무난해요. 자기 이야기를 할 때는 편하게 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: It refers to a person doing unskilled physical work, and depending on the listener it can sound belittling. When addressing someone or speaking politely, '일용직 근로자' or '노동자' is safer. People sometimes use it casually about themselves.

examples.en: I did manual labor to earn my college tuition.
During vacation I do manual labor at a construction site.
People who do manual labor are really strong.
I kept studying every night while doing manual labor.
My father raised us by doing manual labor.

examples.ko: 몸이 아파서 더는 막노동할 수 없어요.
examples.en: I'm sick, so I can't do manual labor anymore.

explain: 기술 없이 몸을 써서 하는 일을 할 때 써요. 윗사람 일에는 '막노동하시다'로 높이지만, 부드럽게 말할 때는 '공사장에서 일하다', '일용직으로 일하다'처럼 바꿔 말하기도 해요. 일의 종류보다 힘든 몸일이라는 느낌이 강해요.
explain_en: It is used when doing work with your body without special skills. For elders you honor it as '막노동하시다', and to soften it people say things like '공사장에서 일하다' or '일용직으로 일하다'. It stresses the hard physical nature of the work more than the kind of job.
